newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton mixed on lower supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton mixed on lower supply.

text.p: Indian cotton was mixed on Tuesday with Punjab varieties rising on reduced arrivals and Gujarat falling on profit-taking, dealers said.

Punjab cotton extended gains on shortage of ready stock following reducing arrivals in producing centres, traders said. Daily average arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region have gone down to 4,000/5,000 bales (170 kg each).
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose 5 rupees to 1,575/1,670 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), traders said.
Bengal-deshi rose by the same margin to 880/935 rupees per maund while cotton F-414 settled 5 rupees higher at 1,885/1,905 rupees per maund.
"Gujarat cotton lost ground on profit-taking following fresh arrivals as unseasonal rain petered out," one trader said.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) moved down by 100 rupees to 13,600/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg), traders said.
Cotton prices were firm last week on reduced arrivals due to unseasonal rains in the different producing centres of India.
